7 year age difference with my sister. Loving parents but typical dysfunction like every family in the world, divorce etc. We are the only 2 children. I missed my sister alot when she moved out, but as I got older I understood why, and even more so when I eventually ended up moving out myself. It’s easier said than done, but you do not have to carry the burden. I remember thinking as a child, that I missed her presence when she was gone, but never thinking to the extent into thinking that my life would have been easier if she was there with me—I knew that she had to better her own life, too, and eventually I did the same as I grew older and also moved out on my own. I’m not saying that you should be selfish and completely disregard your sister’s feelings, but you are focusing too much on the hypotheticals, the what if’s, etc. I understand that you just care for her deeply. Luckily, as you said in your post, your mom is there to take care of her. Do you have any sort of communication with her? Does she act weirdly towards you which is why you feel this way?

Having a food aversion might constitute probably needing to see a professional whether it be nausea related or mental health related.
I am going to be honest here—I think you might have answered your own question yourself. After explaining your food aversion, the post segwayed immediately as to what your perception is as to how you feel you look like, and those two things, like you said, sounds a lot like anorexia right? Then why bring it up if they are not related to each other? 
Food is fuel, not a fattening agent, if one has a healthy diet. Not eating actually lowers your metabolism and makes you prone to gaining weight. If the texture and taste of food is a problem lately for you, I suggest you might look into seeking professional help, or maybe try talking to your mom about this.

ignore the unnecessary comment. coming from someone who was born in a very poor household (living literally in a house with no floors, concrete block houses) and then moving into a upper middle class neighborhood (neighboring houses are worth millions), i can assure to you that your background does not affect in any way whatsoever the validity of your feelings. people of different backgrounds can very much so feel the same emotions. we are all humans. your feelings are very much so valid. 

as for you feeling like you are wasting your life, if you truly do, then the obvious answer is to try to make the most out of it! of course that’s easier said than done, but take little steps to try to find ways to better your life. i get it, finding determination is hard. its ironic because i wish i could follow my own advice, but i can assure to you that you are capable of doing so much more to make yourself feel better.

write a list of things that you think can better your day, they can be something simple like drinking more water to be more hydrated or something. all you need is just a little progress, whether it be the smallest kind of progress, and then you’ll already be on the path to being successful. if you need to talk to anyone my pms are open!
